title: Review of c26's eco-lenia2 (IXDE) on fresh seed 3: competition delays species A (20 cells at t=278 vs 128 in the separate-food twin), A divides (12 persistent splits, generation 3), and a local food cut kills one A cell (and one B cell) within 20-25 t while the fed twins persist; E by construction
summary: Re-ran world.py and its SEP=1 twin (own food field per species, no exclusion) on seed 3 (160^2, t=1000), and the claim's cutfork.py on one median A cell and one median B cell at t=400 with the fed twin in lockstep. Competition: A reaches 20 cells at t=278 (twin 128), averages 14.6 cells over t=100-400 (twin 26.5), and both arms end near 30 (28 vs 31 at t=600); B gains (57.4 vs 50.4 cells over t>=300). A: 12 persistent splits, generation 3 (twin 12, generation 4), merge/split 0.80. Cuts: the A target falls below 10% of its matter at t=420 and to 0 by t=450, while the fed twin keeps 104%; the B target falls below 10% at t=425 (fed twin 100%); domain counts stay within 1-3 cells of the fed twin. The claim replicates.

observations.I: pack_s3_species.png: discrete round A cells (orange) persisting between divisions, 21.7 on average
observations.X: acount.txt: A reaches 20 cells at t=278 with competition vs 128 in the matched separate-food twin; A mean t=100-400 14.6 vs 26.5; B 57.4 vs 50.4
observations.D: pack/FACTS.md species A: 12 persistent splits, max generation 3
observations.E: cuts/cutA_s3.png and cutA_s3.json: food held at 0 in a 12 px disk around one A cell at t=400: below 10% at t=420, fed twin 104%; cutB_s3: B cell below 10% at t=425, fed twin 100%

seeds_run.result: pass: X (t20 278 vs 128), D (12 persistent splits, gen 3), E (local cut kills A and B targets in 20-25 t, fed twins persist)

verdicts.track_note: All A cells descend from the one planted founder; the cut A cell is one of them and grows in competition with B

controls_run.E: cuts/cutA_s3.json, cuts/cutB_s3.json (local cut with fed twin)

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (matter is built only from food and decays). Founders are planted Chan replicators, so reproduction is Chan's and S is not claimed. Part of X comes from a coded exclusion term (growth x (1 - other's occupancy)); the claim's decomposition attributes the rest to food sharing, which I did not re-run. The X effect is on the growth phase: both arms reach ~30 A cells by t=600. One fresh seed.
